subject: Crescent Health — proposed security exhibit cadence + legal redline kanban
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortiz <procurement@crescenthealth.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Crescent Health — draft security exhibit + suggested cadence (kanban attached)

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attaching a first-pass security exhibit and an evidence matrix. High level:

- We preserved the standard SOC 2 assertions and added a short section that describes our evidence cadence (quarterly package + live logs on request with 30-day SLA).
- For penetration testing, the proposed compromise language is: "Customer may request an on-demand penetration test once per 12-month period; Redwood will coordinate scheduling and provide test windows within a mutually agreed 30-day window. Redwood will provide scoped staging access for whitebox testing where applicable."

To keep legal moving quickly, I spun up a short kanban board (link below) with three lanes: Legal redlines, Engineering gating, and Provisioning. Each lane has discrete owners and target completion dates. Can you confirm your preferred pen-test window timing (Q3 preferred) and whether the SOC 2 evidence cadence quarterly package is acceptable as described?

Attachments: Crescent_Security_Exhibit_Draft_v1.docx, evidence_matrix_vC.xlsx, pen_test_window_proposal.pdf

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Ortiz <procurement@crescenthealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Crescent Health — draft security exhibit + suggested cadence (kanban attached)

Hannah — appreciate the quick turnaround and the kanban. A couple of asks from our side:

1) Our security team prefers annual pen tests aligned to our internal calendar (we target September). Can Redwood commit to a fixed 30-day scheduling SLA once we lock dates?
2) For SOC 2 evidence: quarterly is fine, but we need proof of log retention for 13 months for audit purposes. Can you confirm retention windows and whether logs can be exported to our S3 for the audit window?

If you can get Laura on a short call this afternoon to walk legal through a few redlines (MSA §6.4 re: audit rights; Order Form appendix on inspection), that would be great.

— Jamie
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortiz <procurement@crescenthealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Crescent Health — draft security exhibit + suggested cadence (kanban attached)

Jamie — thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses and proposed redline language so we can avoid a long back-and-forth: 

1) Pen test scheduling: Redwood can commit to providing a mutually agreed 30-day scheduling window after receipt of formal written notice by Customer. Proposed clause: "Upon Customer's written request, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule an external penetration test within thirty (30) days; if testing requires staging access, Redwood will provide scoped access and temporary credentials under an agreed access plan."

2) Log retention/export: We confirm retention of audit logs for 13 months. For exports, we can provide an S3 export with limited-scope log bundles for the audit period under a one-time export fee (listed in Order Form Appendix B) or provide read-only console access to a subset of logs under an NDA. Proposed clause: "Redwood retains operational logs for a minimum of 395 days and will, upon Customer request, export a scoped log bundle to Customer's provided S3 bucket or provide read-only access for the audit period."

3) MSA §6.4 (inspection rights): We are proposing to limit on-site physical inspections to scheduled events and require a scoping call 14 days in advance; remote evidence review remains standard. Proposed redline attached (see Crescent_Security_Exhibit_Draft_v1.docx).

Next steps: Hannah — can you confirm Engineering availability for a 30-min technical gating call this afternoon so Marissa can map the staging tasks on the kanban? Marcus — can you confirm the retention export format (CSV vs Parquet) and who owns the export job?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Crescent Health — draft security exhibit + suggested cadence (kanban attached)

Laura / team — I can own the export job. Our default export format is Parquet for efficiency; we can also produce CSV on request but it will take longer and increase compute. For the pen test staging: Marissa, can we reserve a 4-hour staging window and a support engineer for the week of Sep 6 (tentative) to coincide with Crescent's September preference? Hannah — I'll add a card on the kanban (Export: Parquet pipeline) with ETA June 10 for a test run.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — that all sounds workable. Confirming: Crescent is targeting week of Sep 6 for the pen test; we'll sign the kanban/ack once Laura's redline language is finalized. Devon (security operations) will coordinate the technical kickoff with Marcus and Marissa next week.

On a practical note: please include the pen-test scope (IPs, endpoints, staging creds) on the kanban card so our security team can pre-authorize tooling.

Best,
Devon Park

Crescent Health
